gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta stands tall, its terminals cut back to leave generous gaps. Offside does the loud work, wire-light curves that never quite close, while the sans-serif body handles the steady talking with its dominant x-height.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic reads friendly and compact, with open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs and hardly any step up to caps. Offside adds flat, modulation-free curves overhead; the two stay clearly apart.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-vai: Offside spaces its letters wide and leaves its curves open, drawn in flat single-weight linework. Noto Sans Vai, a sans, packs words into solid blocks with generous space where curves meet the stem.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Wide-set, unclosed curves and no fuss. Offside keeps its curves full at the shoulders, while Noto Sans Vithkuqi opens its throats and barely steps from capital to lowercase, so the two feel like one unhurried voice.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Expressive and hairline-free, Offside spreads out its curves without ever swelling them. Noto Sans Wancho, a sans-serif, does the heavy lifting below with a hulking lowercase and an e that gapes at the terminal.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Contemporary and clean, Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks, with wide channels leading into each counter. Shrink Offside and its rope-heavy curves quickly lose their command.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-yi: Flat, contrast-free curves up top: Offside is all level strokes, while Noto Sans Yi carries a deep midsection and unlatched rounds. Page after page, the text would feel sturdy and modern.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-sq: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square lifts a soaring x-height over wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Offside's flat, contrast-free letters set a sharply different stage above it.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Level and wide-tracked: Offside matches every curve to its stems. Noto Traditional Nushu fills the line with bowls and a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, so long text would feel friendly.
gen-gf-offside-gf-numans: Offside reads like following a single thread, curves unclosed and letters widely tracked. Numans, the sans-serif here, hangs its s ends far from the spine, and a slightly larger size lets its coiled lowercase breathe.
